conclusions.rationale: Conditioning on S fixes the observations; it does not leave their original uniform law. Choose f_S(x)=1{x in {X_1,...,X_n}}. Its uniform integral is zero while its empirical mean is one. At n=2,t=1/2, the claimed probability bound is 2/e<1 although the probability is one.
conclusions.repair: Use an independent evaluation sample, or supply a valid uniform/data-dependent complexity bound for the selected class.
conclusions.counterexample: For f_S the indicator of the observed finite set, P_n f_S=1 and P f_S=0 for every sample. At n=2,t=1/2 the event has probability one, exceeding 2/e.
